question: If all the letters of the word ABDUCENT are arranged alphabetically, then the position of how many letters will remain unchanged?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The word given is **ABDUCENT**.
 
• When arranged alphabetically, the letters of ABDUCENT will be: **A, B, C, D, E, N, T, U**.
 
• Comparing the original positions: A (1st), B (2nd), C (3rd), D (4th), U (5th), C (6th), E (7th), N (8th), and T (9th), we find that only A and B remain in their original positions.
 
• Therefore, **2 letters** remain unchanged in their positions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alphabetical Order:**

 
 
• Alphabetical order is the sequence in which letters of the alphabet appear.
 
• For example, in alphabetical order, the sequence would be A, B, C, D, and so on up to Z.
 
 
 
• **Position in a Word:**
 
 
• The position of a letter in a word refers to its place in the sequence of letters that make up the word.
 
• For example, in the word "ABDUCENT", A is in the 1st position, B is in the 2nd position, etc.
 
 
 
• **Unchanged Position:**
 
 
• An unchanged position means that the letter remains in the same position even after the word is rearranged alphabetically.
 
• For example, if a letter is in the 1st position in both the original and the rearranged word, it is said to be in an unchanged position.
